subject: dsa
title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
summary: dp[i] is the cheapest cost to reach step i: pay the step's own cost plus the cheaper of the two ways you could have arrived, from one or two steps below. The top sits just past the last step.
problem: Each step has a cost. You climb one or two steps at a time and may start at step 0 or 1. Find the minimum cost to climb past the top.

steps.caption: Each step costs cost[i] to stand on. You climb 1 or 2 at a time, starting at step 0 or 1. Let dp[i] = cheapest cost to reach step i.
dp[0] = 10 and dp[1] = 15: you may start on either bottom step, so reaching it just costs that step itself.
The top is just past the last step, reachable from step 1 or step 2. Its cost is min(dp[1], dp[2]) = min(15, 30).
The cheapest way past the top costs 15: start on step 1, then take a double step over the top.
